lessons.title: स्वर · Vowels
lessons.subtitle: Marathi vowels — same script as Hindi, with Marathi sounds
lessons.content:
# स्वर (Vowels)

Marathi uses the **Devanagari script** (देवनागरी लिपि) — the same script as Hindi and Sanskrit. If you already know Hindi script, you have a head start. But Marathi pronunciation has its own patterns that differ from Hindi in important ways.

## The Vowels (स्वर)

Marathi has the standard Devanagari vowels:

| Vowel | Roman | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| अ | a | अन्न | food |
| आ | ā | आई | mother |
| इ | i | इंद्र | Indra |
| ई | ī | ईश्वर | God |
| उ | u | उन | heat |
| ऊ | ū | ऊन | sunlight |
| ए | e | एक | one |
| ऐ | ai | ऐश्वर्य | wealth |
| ओ | o | ओढ | pull |
| औ | au | औषध | medicine |
| ऋ | ru | ऋण | debt (rare, Sanskrit loans) |

> **Marathi pronunciation note:** Unlike Hindi, where अ and आ are clearly distinct, in casual Marathi speech, inherent अ is often pronounced closer to /ə/ (schwa, like 'a' in 'about'). The long vowels आ, ई, ऊ are clearly long, but short अ, इ, उ can be very brief.

## Short vs Long Distinction

Marathi preserves the short/long distinction more consistently than Bengali:

- अ (a) → आ (ā): अन्न (ann — food) vs आनंद (ānand — joy)
- इ (i) → ई (ī): इंद्र (indr — Indra) vs ईश्वर (īshwar — God)
- उ (u) → ऊ (ū): उन (un — heat) vs ऊन (ūn — sunlight)

> Tip: The long vowels आ, ई, ऊ have the vertical matras (ा, ी, ू) that the short forms lack. This visual cue is the same as in Hindi.

## Reading Practice — Marathi Words

- आई (āī) — mother (Marathi's most common word for mother)
- अन्न (ann) — food / grain
- एक (ek) — one
- ओढ (ōdh) — pull
- औषध (aushadh) — medicine

> **आई (āī)** is the Marathi word for 'mother' — distinct from Hindi's माँ (mā̃) or माता (mātā). This is one of the first words Marathi children learn, and it's a marker of Marathi identity.

## The Inherent Vowel

Like Hindi, a Marathi consonant without a matra carries the inherent 'a':

- क alone = 'ka'
- क + ा (आ matra) = का = 'kā'
- क + ि (इ matra) = कि = 'ki'

This is the same rule as Hindi — if you can read Hindi, you can read Marathi script.

## Cultural Note: Marathi and Devanagari

Marathi has been written in Devanagari since the 13th century. Before that, it was written in **Modi script** (मोडी लिपि) — a cursive script used for administrative records. Modi is still studied by historians but Devanagari is now universal.

> Marathi's Devanagari is nearly identical to Hindi's, but the LANGUAGE is different. The script is shared; the words, grammar, and pronunciation are Marathi.

lessons.title: व्यंजन · Consonants
lessons.subtitle: Marathi consonants — including the unique retroflex ळ
lessons.content:
# व्यंजन (Consonants)

Marathi has the standard Devanagari consonants plus one very special sound: **ळ (ḷ)** — the retroflex lateral. This sound is unique to Marathi among major Indian languages and is a key marker of Marathi identity.

## The Standard Consonant Groups

### क-वर्ग (Velars)
क (ka), ख (kha), ग (ga), घ (gha), ङ (ṅa — rare)

### च-वर्ग (Palatals)
च (cha), छ (chha), ज (ja), झ (jha), ञ (ña — rare)

### ट-वर्ग (Retroflex)
ट (ṭa), ठ (ṭha), ड (ḍa), ढ (ḍha), ण (ṇa)

### त-वर्ग (Dentals)
त (ta), थ (tha), द (da), ध (dha), न (na)

### प-वर्ग (Labials)
प (pa), फ (pha), ब (ba), भ (bha), म (ma)

### Semivowels and Sibilants
य (ya), र (ra), ल (la), व (va), श (sha), ष (sha), स (sa), ह (ha)

## The Star of Marathi: ळ (ḷ)

**ळ (ḷ)** is the **retroflex lateral** — a sound made by curling the tongue back and releasing air around the sides. It is:

- **NOT found in Hindi** (Hindi uses ल for everything)
- **NOT found in standard Bengali**
- Found in Marathi, Tamil, Malayalam, and some other Dravidian languages
- A key marker of Marathi identity

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| काळ | kāḷ | time |
| पाळ | pāḷ | to nurture |
| फुलांचा गळ | phulāñchā gaḷ | garland of flowers |
| ळांगळी | ḷāṅgḷī | (a type of lizard) |
| कोळी | koḷī | fisherman (community name) |

> Tip: To pronounce ळ, say 'la' but with your tongue curled back to the roof of your mouth (the same position as for ट or ड). It sounds thicker and more resonant than regular ल. If you can't get it right away, practice with the word **काळ** (kāḷ — time) — one of the most common Marathi words.

## When to Use ळ vs ल

This is a key spelling challenge in Marathi. Many words that have ल in Hindi have ळ in Marathi:

| Hindi | Marathi | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| काल | काळ | time |
| फल | फळ | fruit |
| जल | जळ | water (poetic) |
| बाल | बाळ | child |
| चाल | चाळ | sieve |
| माल | माळ | garland |

> If you know Hindi, watch for this pattern: many Hindi words with ल become ळ in Marathi. This is one of the easiest ways to identify Marathi text.

## Marathi's Three Sibilants

Like Hindi, Marathi has three sibilants — but unlike Bengali (where they all merge to /ʃ/), Marathi preserves a distinction:

- **श (śa)** — /ʃ/ like 'sh' in 'ship' — most common
- **ष (ṣa)** — retroflex /ʂ/ — used in Sanskrit loans (कृष्ण, षष्ठ)
- **स (sa)** — /s/ like 's' in 'sit' — common in native words

> Marathi keeps these three sounds distinct, unlike Bengali. सडक (sadak — road) vs शहर (shahar — city) — clearly different sounds.

## The Distinctive Marathi Pronunciation

Some consonants have Marathi-specific pronunciation patterns:

- **ज (ja):** In Marathi, often pronounced /dʒ/ (like 'j' in 'jump') — same as Hindi
- **व (va):** In Marathi, sometimes pronounced /w/ in the middle of words — softer than Hindi
- **च (cha):** Always /tʃ/ (like 'ch' in 'chair')

> Marathi's consonant system is very close to Hindi's — if you can pronounce Hindi, you can pronounce Marathi consonants. The biggest difference is ळ, which doesn't exist in Hindi.

## Reading Practice

Try these Marathi words with ळ:

- काळ (kāḷ) — time
- फळ (phaḷ) — fruit
- बाळ (bāḷ) — child
- कोळी (koḷī) — fisherman
- पाळ (pāḷ) — to raise/nurture

> The ळ sound is a badge of Marathi identity. When you hear someone use काळ instead of काल, you know they're speaking Marathi, not Hindi.

lessons.title: मात्रा · Vowel Signs
lessons.subtitle: How vowels attach to consonants in Marathi
lessons.content:
# मात्रा (Vowel Signs)

Marathi matras work exactly like Hindi matras — the same Devanagari system. If you know Hindi matras, you know Marathi matras.

## The Matras

| Vowel | Matra | Consonant + Matra | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| अ (a) | (none) | क | ka |
| आ (ā) | ा | का | kā |
| इ (i) | ि | कि | ki |
| ई (ī) | ी | की | kī |
| उ (u) | ु | कु | ku |
| ऊ (ū) | ू | कू | kū |
| ए (e) | े | के | ke |
| ऐ (ai) | ै | कै | kai |
| ओ (o) | ो | को | ko |
| औ (au) | ौ | कौ | kau |
| ऋ (ru) | ृ | कृ | kru |

> Note: The matra for short 'i' (ि) goes to the **LEFT** of the consonant but is read AFTER. So कि is read 'ki', not 'ik'. All other matras go to the right.

## Reading Practice — Marathi Words

| Word | Breakdown | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| आई | आ + ई | ā-ī | mother |
| बाबा | बा + ब + ा | bā-bā | father |
| भाजी | भा + ज + ी | bhā-jī | vegetable |
| पोळी | पो + ळ + ी | po-ḷ-ī | bread (flatbread) |
| वडा | व + ड + ा | va-ḍā | snack (vada) |
| अन्न | अ + न + ् + न | an-n | food |

> **भाजी (bhājī)** is Marathi for 'vegetable' — different from Hindi's सब्ज़ी (sabzī). **पोळी (poḷī)** is the Marathi word for the flatbread that Hindi calls रोटी (roṭī). These are core Marathi vocabulary.

## The Halant (्) — Virama

The mark ् (halant) cancels the inherent vowel:

- क + ् + ष + ट = क्ष (kṣa)
- त + ् + र = त्र (tra)
- ज + ् + ञ = ज्ञ (jña)
- न + ् + न = न्न (nn — as in अन्न)

> In Marathi, ज्ञ is pronounced /dʒɲ/ (jñ) — closer to the Sanskrit pronunciation than Hindi's /gy/ or Bengali's /ggy/. So ज्ञान (knowledge) is 'jñān' in Marathi, 'gyān' in Hindi, 'ggyan' in Bengali.

## Common Conjuncts in Marathi

| Conjunct | Written | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| क + ष | क्ष | क्षत्रिय | warrior |
| त + र | त्र | त्रिशूल | trident |
| ज + ञ | ज्ञ | ज्ञान | knowledge |
| श + र | श्र | श्रीमान | sir |
| न + न | न्न | अन्न | food |
| ळ (with matra) | ळी | पोळी | flatbread |

> The न्न conjunct (as in अन्न — food) is very common in Marathi. It's a doubled 'n' sound, held longer than a single न.

## Writing Practice

Try writing these Marathi words:

1. **āī** (mother) → आई
2. **bābā** (father) → बाबा
3. **bhājī** (vegetable) → भाजी
4. **poḷī** (flatbread) → पोळी
5. **vaḍā** (snack) → वडा
6. **kāḷ** (time) → काळ

> Notice the ळ in पोळी and काळ — this is the distinctive Marathi sound. If you write पोली instead of पोळी, a Marathi speaker will notice immediately.

lessons.title: बाराखडी · Consonant + Vowel Combinations
lessons.subtitle: The full grid of consonant-vowel combinations
lessons.content:
# बाराखडी (Barakhadi)

The **बाराखडी** is the grid of one consonant combined with each vowel. Mastering this for a few consonants unlocks reading any Marathi word.

## क Barakhadi

| Consonant + Vowel | Written | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| क + अ | क | ka |
| क + आ | का | kā |
| क + इ | कि | ki |
| क + ई | की | kī |
| क + उ | कु | ku |
| क + ऊ | कू | kū |
| क + ए | के | ke |
| क + ऐ | कै | kai |
| क + ओ | को | ko |
| क + औ | कौ | kau |
| क + ऋ | कृ | kru |

## ळ Barakhadi (Marathi's Special Consonant)

| Consonant + Vowel | Written | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| ळ + अ | ळ | ḷa |
| ळ + आ | ळा | ḷā |
| ळ + इ | ळि | ḷi |
| ळ + ई | ळी | ḷī |
| ळ + उ | ळु | ḷu |
| ळ + ऊ | ळू | ḷū |
| ळ + ए | ळे | ḷe |
| ळ + ऐ | ळै | ḷai |
| ळ + ओ | ळो | ḷo |
| ळ + औ | ळौ | ḷau |

> Practice the ळ barakhadi — it's uniquely Marathi. Words like काळ (time), फळ (fruit), बाळ (child) use this consonant.

## Reading Practice — Real Marathi Words

- आई (āī) — mother
- बाबा (bābā) — father
- भाजी (bhājī) — vegetable
- पोळी (poḷī) — flatbread
- वडा (vaḍā) — fried snack
- अन्न (ann) — food
- गाणं (gāṇa) — song
- नमस्कार (namaskār) — hello
- काळ (kāḷ) — time
- शाळा (shāḷā) — school

> Notice how many core Marathi words use ळ: पोळी, काळ, शाळा. This is a quick way to identify Marathi text vs Hindi.

## The Anusvara (ं)

The dot above the line (ं) nasalises the following consonant:

- गाणं (gāṇa) — song: the ं nasalises the final sound
- अन्न (ann) — food: no anusvara, just doubled न
- संग (sanga) — company: ं = /ng/ before ग

> In Marathi, ं at the END of a word often indicates a nasalised vowel (like गाणं — the final अ is nasalised). This is similar to Hindi's ँ (chandrabindu).

## Writing Practice

Write these Marathi words:

1. **namaskār** (hello) → नमस्कार
2. **bhājī** (vegetable) → भाजी
3. **poḷī** (flatbread) → पोळी
4. **kāḷ** (time) → काळ
5. **gāṇa** (song) → गाणं
6. **shāḷā** (school) → शाळा

> These are foundational Marathi words. If you can write and read them, you've taken a big step toward Marathi literacy.

lessons.title: संयुक्त व्यंजन · Conjunct Consonants
lessons.subtitle: Two consonants joined without a vowel
lessons.content:
# संयुक्त व्यंजन (Conjunct Consonants)

When two consonants appear together without a vowel between them, they form a **conjunct** (संयुक्त). The **halant** (्) cancels the inherent vowel. Marathi conjuncts are the same as Hindi/Sanskrit conjuncts since the script is shared.

## Common Conjuncts

| Conjunct | Written | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| क + ष | क्ष | क्षत्रिय | warrior |
| त + र | त्र | त्रिशूल | trident |
| ज + ञ | ज्ञ | ज्ञान | knowledge |
| श + र | श्र | श्रीमान | sir |
| न + न | न्न | अन्न | food |
| न + द | न्द | आनंद | joy |
| म + न | म्न | प्रम्न | (rare) |
| क + त | क्त | भक्त | devotee |
| ष + ट | ष्ट | षष्ठ | sixth |
| द + व | द्व | द्वार | door |

## The Marathi Pronunciation of ज्ञ

A key difference from Hindi:

- **Marathi:** ज्ञ = /dʒɲ/ (jñ) — closer to Sanskrit
  - ज्ञान (jñān) — knowledge
- **Hindi:** ज्ञ = /gy/ (gy)
  - ज्ञान (gyān) — knowledge
- **Bengali:** জ্ঞ = /ggyo/ (ggyo)
  - জ্ঞান (ggyan) — knowledge

> If you know Hindi, you need to adjust your pronunciation of ज्ञ. In Marathi, it's 'jñ' (a 'j' sound followed by a 'ñ' sound), not 'gy'.

## Reading Practice — Common Marathi Words

- **नमस्कार** (namaskār) — hello: न + म + स + ् + क + ा + र
- **आनंद** (ānand) — joy: आ + न + ं + द
- **प्रेम** (prem) — love: प + ् + र + े + म
- **मित्र** (mitra) — friend: म + ि + त + ् + र
- **अन्न** (ann) — food: अ + न + ् + न
- **भक्त** (bhakt) — devotee: भ + क + ् + त
- **द्वार** (dvār) — door: द + ् + व + ा + र

> Note: नमस्कार uses स + ् + क = स्क conjunct. This is the same as Hindi's नमस्ते structurally, but Marathi uses कार (kār) ending instead of ते (te).

## The Anusvara (ं) vs Halant (्)

Two different marks with different functions:

- **ं (anusvara):** nasalises the FOLLOWING consonant. संग (sanga) — the ं makes the ग nasal.
- **् (halant):** cancels the inherent vowel. अन्न (ann) — the ् joins two न's without a vowel.

> In Marathi, आनंद (joy) uses anusvara (ं before द), while अन्न (food) uses halant (् between two न's). Both create 'doubled' sounds but through different mechanisms.

## The Visarga (ः)

The visarga (ः) — two dots after a vowel — adds a breathy 'h':

- दुःख (duḥkha) — sorrow
- पुण्य (puṇya) — merit (note: no visarga here, just ण)
- अतिथि (atithi) — guest (no visarga)

> Visarga is rare in everyday Marathi, appearing mainly in Sanskrit loanwords. Most Marathi words don't use it.

## Reading Marathi Sentences

Try reading this short sentence:

> मी मराठी शिकतो।
> (mī marāṭhī shikato.)
> I learn Marathi. (male speaker)

Breakdown:
- मी (mī) — I
- मराठी (marāṭhī) — Marathi (the language)
- शिकतो (shikato) — learn (male speaker)

> Notice: शिकतो ends in �ो — this is the Marathi masculine present-tense ending. Hindi would use ता हूँ (shikhtā hū̃). Marathi packs the verb into one word.

lessons.title: नमस्कार · Greetings
lessons.subtitle: Marathi greetings — नमस्कार and beyond
lessons.content:
# नमस्कार (Greetings)

Marathi greetings center on **नमस्कार (namaskār)** — the universal Marathi greeting. While similar to Hindi's नमस्ते, Marathi prefers नमस्कार with the कार ending. Choosing the right greeting shows cultural awareness.

## The Universal Greeting

**नमस्कार (namaskār)** is used in any context — formal, informal, with elders, with peers:

- नमस्कार। — Hello. / Greetings.
- नमस्कार, कसे आहात? — Hello, how are you? (to a male, respectful)
- नमस्कार, कशी आहात? — Hello, how are you? (to a female, respectful)

> **नमस्कार** vs **नमस्कार**: Marathi consistently uses नमस्कार (with कार), while Hindi uses नमस्कार (same spelling) or नमस्ते. The words look identical but Marathi speakers gravitate toward नमस्कार as the default.

## Time-Based Greetings

| Time | Greeting | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | सुप्रभात | Good morning (formal) |
| Morning | शुभ सकाळ | Good morning |
| Noon | शुभ दुपार | Good afternoon |
| Evening | शुभ संध्याकाळ | Good evening |
| Night | शुभ रात्री | Good night |

> In everyday speech, Marathi speakers simply use नमस्कार regardless of time. The time-specific greetings are more formal/literary.

## Informal Greetings

Between friends and peers:

- **हाय (hāy)** — Hi (borrowed from English)
- **कसा आहेस? (kasā ahes?)** — How are you? (to a male, informal)
- **कशी आहेस? (kaśī ahes?)** — How are you? (to a female, informal)
- **काय चालू आहे? (kāy chālū ahe?)** — What's going on? / What's up?

## Formal/Respectful Greetings

When addressing elders or in formal contexts:

- **तुम्ही कसे आहात? (tumhī kase āhāt?)** — How are you? (to a male, respectful)
- **तुम्ही कशी आहात? (tumhī kaśī āhāt?)** — How are you? (to a female, respectful)
- **आपण कसे आहात? (āpaṇ kase āhāt?)** — How are you? (very formal/respectful)

## The Three 'You's in Marathi

Marathi has THREE levels of 'you', similar to Hindi but with different words:

1. **तू (tū)** — intimate. For close friends, younger family, children. Singular.
2. **तुम्ही (tumhī)** — familiar/respectful. For peers, elders, strangers. Grammatically plural.
3. **आपण (āpaṇ)** — very formal. For elders, in-laws, respected figures. Grammatically plural.

> This is similar to Hindi's तू/तुम/आप system, but the Marathi words are different. Note: तुम्ही is more commonly used than Hindi's तुम — it carries respect, not just familiarity.

## Common Responses

- **मी ठीक आहे (mī ṭhīk ahe)** — I am fine (male speaker)
- **मी ठीक आहे (mī ṭhīk ahe)** — I am fine (female speaker — same!)
- **खूप छान (khūp chhān)** — Very nice / very good
- **थोडं थकलो (thodaṃ thaklo)** — A bit tired (male)
- **थोडं थकले (thodaṃ thakle)** — A bit tired (female/neuter)

> Marathi verb agreement changes by GENDER of the subject, like Hindi. But Marathi has THREE genders (masculine, feminine, neuter) while Hindi has only two. You'll learn more about this in the grammar chapter.

## Parting Phrases

- **पुन्हा भेटूया (punhā bheṭūyā)** — Let's meet again
- **येतो (yeto)** — I'm leaving (informal, male)
- **येते (yete)** — I'm leaving (female/neuter)
- **बाय (bāy)** — Bye (borrowed from English)
- **सावधान (sāvdhān)** — Take care (literally: be alert)

## Cultural Note: The Namaskar Gesture

When saying नमस्कार, Marathi people join their palms at the chest (the **añjali mudrā**) and slightly bow. This gesture accompanies the word. The gesture is the same across Hindi, Marathi, and other Indian cultures — it's a pan-Indian sign of respect.

> In Maharashtra, when greeting an elder, it's common to touch their feet (पाय लागणे — pāy lāgṇe) — a gesture of deep respect. This is especially common in traditional families.

## Practice

Match the greeting to the context:

1. Greeting your teacher → नमस्कार, आपण कसे आहात?
2. Greeting a male friend → हाय, कसा आहेस?
3. Greeting a female friend → हाय, कशी आहेस?
4. Saying goodbye → पुन्हा भेटूया
5. Answering "how are you?" → मी ठीक आहे

lessons.title: माझं नाव · Introductions
lessons.subtitle: Introducing yourself in Marathi
lessons.content:
# परिचय (Introductions)

Marathi introductions follow the SOV pattern (Subject-Object-Verb). Once you know the key phrases, you can introduce yourself and ask about others.

## Introducing Yourself

- **माझं नाव ... आहे (mājhaṃ nāv ... ahe)** — My name is ...
- **मी ... (mī ...)** — I am ...

Examples:
- माझं नाव राहुल आहे। — My name is Rahul.
- मी अनिता। — I am Anita.
- माझं नाव सारा आहे, मी अमेरिकेतून आले आहे। — My name is Sara, I have come from America.

> Marathi sentences end with the verb. **आहे (ahe)** means 'is' / 'am' (neuter form — used when the subject is 'I' regardless of the speaker's gender, because नाव 'name' is neuter).

## Asking Names

- **तुमचं नाव काय? (tumchaṃ nāv kāy?)** — What is your name? (respectful)
- **तुझं नाव काय? (tujhaṃ nāv kāy?)** — What is your name? (informal)

> **Possessive forms:** माझं (mājhaṃ — my, neuter), तुमचं (tumchaṃ — your, respectful, neuter), तुझं (tujhaṃ — your, informal, neuter). The form is neuter because नाव (name) is a neuter noun in Marathi.

## Where Are You From?

- **तुम्ही कोठून आहात? (tumhī koṭhūn āhāt?)** — Where are you from? (respectful)
- **तू कोठून आहेस? (tū koṭhūn āhes?)** — Where are you from? (informal)

Responses:
- **मी मुंबईतून आहे। (mī mumbaītūn ahe.)** — I am from Mumbai.
- **मी महाराष्ट्रातून आहे। (mī mahārāṣṭrātūn ahe.)** — I am from Maharashtra.
- **मी पुण्याहून आले आहे। (mī puṇyāhūn āle ahe.)** — I have come from Pune.

> The postposition **-हून (-hūn)** means 'from': मुंबई + हून = मुंबईतून (from Mumbai). This is different from Hindi's से (se).

## What Do You Do?

- **तुम्ही काय करता? (tumhī kāy kartā?)** — What do you do? (to a male, respectful)
- **तुम्ही काय करता? (tumhī kāy kartā?)** — What do you do? (to a female, respectful — same question, different verb agreement in answer)

Responses:
- **मी विद्यार्थी आहे। (mī vidyārthī ahe.)** — I am a student. (male)
- **मी विद्यार्थिनी आहे। (mī vidyārthinī ahe.)** — I am a student. (female)
- **मी शिक्षक आहे। (mī shikṣak ahe.)** — I am a teacher. (male)
- **मी शिक्षिका आहे। (mī shikṣikā ahe.)** — I am a teacher. (female)

> Marathi marks gender on some nouns (विद्यार्थी/विद्यार्थिनी, शिक्षक/शिक्षिका) — similar to Hindi. But Marathi also has a NEUTER gender that Hindi lacks, which you'll learn about in the grammar chapter.

## Full Introduction Example

> नमस्कार! माझं नाव विक्रम आहे। मी पुण्यात राहतो। मी अभियंता आहे। तुमच्या भेटीचा आनंद आहे।
>
> Hello! My name is Vikram. I live in Pune. I am an engineer. Nice to meet you.

**तुमच्या भेटीचा आनंद आहे (tumachyā bhetīchā ānand ahe)** — 'meeting you is a joy' — is a formal way to say 'nice to meet you'. In casual speech, Marathi speakers might just say **भेटायला छान झालं (bheṭāyalā chhān jhalaṃ)** — 'nice to meet'.

## Common Professions

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| विद्यार्थी / विद्यार्थिनी | vidyārthī / vidyārthinī | student (m/f) |
| शिक्षक / शिक्षिका | shikṣak / shikṣikā | teacher (m/f) |
| डॉक्टर | ḍākṭar | doctor |
| अभियंता | abhiyantā | engineer |
| शेतकरी | shetkarī | farmer |
| व्यापारी | vyāpārī | businessman |
| लेखक / लेखिका | lekhak / lekhikā | writer (m/f) |
| कलाकार | kalākār | artist |
| कामगार | kāmgār | worker |
| गृहिणी | gruhiṇī | housewife |

## Asking About Family

- **तुमच्या कुटुंबात कोण कोण आहे? (tumachyā kuṭumbāt koṇ koṇ ahe?)** — Who is in your family?
- **तुमचे भाऊ-बहीण काय करतात? (tumache bhāu-bahīṇ kāy kartāt?)** — What do your siblings do?

## Practice

Construct your own introduction:

1. माझं नाव _____ आहे। — My name is _____.
2. मी _____-त राहतो/राहते। — I live in _____.
3. मी _____ आहे। — I am a _____ (profession).

lessons.title: कुटुंब · Family
lessons.subtitle: Marathi kinship terms — distinct from Hindi
lessons.content:
# कुटुंब (Family)

Marathi kinship terms are distinct from Hindi. While some overlap exists (both languages use Sanskrit-derived terms), Marathi has its own words for core family relationships.

## Immediate Family

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| आई | āī | mother |
| बाबा / वडील | bābā / vaḍīl | father |
| भाऊ | bhāu | brother |
| बहीण | bahīṇ | sister |
| मुलगा | mulgā | son |
| मुलगी | mulgī | daughter |
| पती | patī | husband |
| पत्नी | patnī | wife |

> **आई (āī)** is the Marathi word for 'mother' — distinct from Hindi's माँ (mā̃). This is one of the first words Marathi children learn. **बाबा (bābā)** is the affectionate word for 'father'; **वडील (vaḍīl)** is the formal word.

## Grandparents

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| आजोबा | ājobā | grandfather |
| आजी | ājī | grandmother |

> Marathi uses आजोबा / आजी for BOTH paternal and maternal grandparents — unlike Hindi which distinguishes दादा/दादी (paternal) from नाना/नानी (maternal). If Marathi speakers need to specify, they say आजोबा (father's side) vs मामाचे आजोबा (mother's father, literally 'uncle's grandfather').

## Uncles and Aunts — Marathi Specific

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| काका | kākā | father's brother |
| काकू | kākū | father's brother's wife |
| मामा | māmā | mother's brother |
| मावशी | māvshī | mother's sister |
| आत्या | ātyā | father's sister |
| मामी | māmī | mother's brother's wife |

> Marathi's kinship is somewhat simpler than Hindi's. काका (uncle) and काकू (aunt) are used broadly for the father's side, while मामा / मावशी / मामी cover the mother's side.

## Older Siblings

Unlike Bengali, Marathi does NOT have separate words for older vs younger siblings. **भाऊ** (brother) and **बहीण** (sister) are used for all siblings regardless of age. If you need to specify, you say:

- थोरले भाऊ (thorle bhāu) — older brother
- धाकटे भाऊ (dhākaṭe bhāu) — younger brother

> This is different from Bengali, where দাদা/দিদি (older brother/sister) are the default terms.

## Talking About Family

- **माझे वडील डॉक्टर आहेत। (māje vaḍīl ḍākṭar āhāt.)** — My father is a doctor.
- **माझ्या आई शिक्षिका आहे। (mājhyā āī shikṣikā ahe.)** — My mother is a teacher.
- **माझे दोन भाऊ आहेत। (māje don bhāu āhāt.)** — I have two brothers.
- **मला एक बहीण आहे। (malā ek bahīṇ ahe.)** — I have one sister.
- **आम्ही पाच जण आहोत। (āmhī pāch jaṇ āhot.)** — We are five people.

> Notice the possessive: **माझे (māje)** before plural/respectful masculine nouns (वडील, भाऊ), **माझ्या (mājhyā)** before feminine nouns (आई, बहीण). This is the Marathi equivalent of Hindi's मेरे / मेरी distinction, but with Marathi-specific forms.

## Asking About Family

- **तुमच्या कुटुंबात कोण कोण आहे? (tumachyā kuṭumbāt koṇ koṇ ahe?)** — Who is in your family?
- **तुमचे किती भाऊ-बहीण आहेत? (tumache kitī bhāu-bahīṇ āhāt?)** — How many siblings do you have?

## Cultural Note: The Joint Family

Maharashtra has a strong tradition of the **संयुक्त कुटुंब (sanyukta kuṭumba — joint family)**, where multiple generations live together. While urbanization has led to more nuclear families, the joint family remains culturally important. Terms like आजोबा / आजी reflect this multi-generational structure.

## Sample Description

> आमचं कुटुंब मोठं आहे। आजोबा, आजी, बाबा-आई, माझे दोन भाऊ, एक बहीण आणि मी — सगळे एकत्र राहतो। माझे थोरले भाऊ अभियंता आहेत आणि माझी बहीण डॉक्टर आहे। मी अजून शिकतो आहे।
>
> Our family is big. Grandfather, grandmother, father-mother, my two brothers, one sister, and I — all live together. My older brother is an engineer and my sister is a doctor. I am still studying.

lessons.title: अंक · Numbers
lessons.subtitle: Marathi numbers — Devanagari with some distinct names
lessons.content:
# अंक (Numbers)

Marathi uses Devanagari numerals (०-९) — the same as Hindi. However, some number names are distinctly Marathi and differ from Hindi.

## Devanagari Numerals

| Digit | Devanagari | Name |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ० | शून्य (śūnya) |
| 1 | १ | एक (ek) |
| 2 | २ | दोन (don) |
| 3 | ३ | तीन (tīn) |
| 4 | ४ | चार (chār) |
| 5 | ५ | पंच (panch) |
| 6 | ६ | षण्ण (ṣaṇṇ) |
| 7 | ७ | सात (sāt) |
| 8 | ८ | आठ (āṭh) |
| 9 | ९ | नऊ (nau) |

> **Marathi differences from Hindi:** 
> - 2: दोन (don) vs Hindi दो (do)
> - 5: पंच (panch) vs Hindi पाँच (pā̃c)
> - 6: षण्ण (ṣaṇṇ) vs Hindi छह (chah) — very different!
> - 9: नऊ (nau) vs Hindi नौ (nau) — close but spelled differently

## 1–10

| Number | Marathi | Hindi | Roman |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | एक | एक | ek |
| 2 | दोन | दो | don |
| 3 | तीन | तीन | tīn |
| 4 | चार | चार | chār |
| 5 | पंच | पाँच | panch |
| 6 | षण्ण | छह | ṣaṇṇ |
| 7 | सात | सात | sāt |
| 8 | आठ | आठ | āṭh |
| 9 | नऊ | नौ | nau |
| 10 | दहा | दस | dahā |

> **षण्ण (ṣaṇṇ — 6)** is one of the most distinctive Marathi number words. It's completely different from Hindi's छह. This is a quick way to identify Marathi speech.

## 11–20

| Number | Marathi | Roman |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | अकरा | akrā |
| 12 | बारा | bārā |
| 13 | तेरा | terā |
| 14 | चौदा | caudā |
| 15 | पंधरा | pandharā |
| 16 | सोळा | soḷā |
| 17 | सतरा | satrā |
| 18 | अठरा | aṭharā |
| 19 | एकोणीस | ekoṇīs |
| 20 | वीस | vīs |

> Marathi 11-18 end in -आ (-ā), unlike Hindi's -रह (-rah). अकरा (11) vs Hindi ग्यारह (11). The 'one less' pattern appears at 19: एकोणीस (one less than twenty).

## Tens (10–100)

| Number | Marathi | Roman |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | दहा | dahā |
| 20 | वीस | vīs |
| 30 | तीस | tīs |
| 40 | चाळीस | chāḷīs |
| 50 | पन्नास | pannās |
| 60 | साठ | sāṭh |
| 70 | सत्तर | sattar |
| 80 | ऐंशी | aiṃśī |
| 90 | नव्व्याणू | navvyāṇū |
| 100 | शंभर | śambhar |

> **शंभर (śambhar — 100)** is distinctly Marathi, different from Hindi's सौ (sau). चाळीस (40) uses the ळ sound — a marker of Marathi.

## Hundreds and Beyond

| Number | Marathi | Roman |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | शंभर | śambhar |
| 200 | दोनशे | donśe |
| 1,000 | हजार | hajār |
| 100,000 | एक लाख | ek lākh |
| 10,000,000 | एक कोटी | ek koṭī |

> Like Hindi and Bengali, Marathi uses लाख (100,000) and कोटी (10,000,000). Note: Marathi says कोटी (koṭī) where Hindi says करोड़ (karoṛ).

## Using Numbers

- **माझे दोन भाऊ आहेत। (māje don bhāu āhāt.)** — I have two brothers.
- **हे पुस्तक पन्नास रुपये आहे। (he pustak pannās rupaye ahe.)** — This book is fifty rupees.
- **मी पुण्यात तीन वर्षं राहिलो। (mī puṇyāt tīn varṣaṃ rāhilo.)** — I lived in Pune for three years.

## Time and Age

- **तो सात वाजता येईल। (to sāt vājtā yeīl.)** — He will come at seven o'clock.
- **मी वीस वर्षांचा आहे। (mī vīs varṣāñchā ahe.)** — I am twenty years old. (male)
- **मी वीस वर्षांची आहे। (mī vīs varṣāñchī ahe.)** — I am twenty years old. (female)

> Note the gender agreement: male says वर्षांचा (varṣāñchā), female says वर्षांची (varṣāñchī). This is similar to Hindi's gender agreement system.

## Practice

Match the number to its Marathi name:

1. 5 → पंच
2. 6 → षण्ण (distinctive Marathi!)
3. 10 → दहा
4. 20 → वीस
5. 100 → शंभर (distinctive Marathi!)

lessons.title: साधे वाक्य · Simple Sentences
lessons.subtitle: SOV word order in Marathi
lessons.content:
# साधे वाक्य (Simple Sentences)

Marathi follows **Subject-Object-Verb (SOV)** word order, like Hindi. The verb always comes last. Marathi verb conjugation is by gender AND number (like Hindi, but with the addition of neuter gender).

## The SOV Pattern

Compare:

- **English (SVO):** I (S) eat (V) rice (O).
- **Marathi (SOV):** मी (S) भात (O) खातो (V)। — I eat rice. (male speaker)

The verb always comes **last**.

## More Examples

| English | Marathi | Word order |
|---|---|---|
| I read a book. | मी पुस्तक वाचतो। | I (S) book (O) read (V) — male |
| I read a book. | मी पुस्तक वाचते। | I (S) book (O) read (V) — female |
| She drinks tea. | ती चहा पिते। | She (S) tea (O) drinks (V) |
| We speak Marathi. | आम्ही मराठी बोलतो। | We (S) Marathi (O) speak (V) |
| They go home. | ते घरी जातात। | They (S) home (O) go (V) |

> **Gender agreement:** मी वाचतो (male speaker) vs मी वाचते (female speaker). The verb ending changes by the speaker's gender. This is similar to Hindi (मैं पढ़ता हूँ vs मैं पढ़ती हूँ) but the endings are different.

## The Verb 'to be' — आहे, आहेस, आहात

The present tense of 'to be' conjugates by person, number, and gender:

| Pronoun | Verb form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| मी (I, male) | आहे (ahe) | मी विद्यार्थी आहे। — I am a student. |
| मी (I, female) | आहे (ahe) | मी विद्यार्थिनी आहे। — I am a student. |
| तू (you, inf., male) | आहेस (āhes) | तू मित्र आहेस। — You are a friend. |
| तू (you, inf., female) | आहेस (āhes) | तू मैत्रिण आहेस। — You are a friend. |
| तुम्ही (you, resp.) | आहात (āhāt) | तुम्ही शिक्षक आहात। — You are a teacher. |
| तो (he) | आहे (ahe) | तो डॉक्टर आहे। — He is a doctor. |
| ती (she) | आहे (ahe) | ती डॉक्टर आहे। — She is a doctor. |
| ते (they / it) | आहेत (āhāt) | ते लोक आहेत। — They are people. |
| आम्ही (we) | आहोत (āhot) | आम्ही मराठी आहोत। — We are Marathi. |

> Note: मी (I) uses आहे regardless of the speaker's gender — but the NOUN changes (विद्यार्थी for male, विद्यार्थिनी for female). The verb agrees with the predicate noun's gender when the subject is मी.

## Simple Statements

Build sentences: **[Subject] [Object/Complement] [Verb]**

- मी + मराठी + आहे = मी मराठी आहे। — I am Marathi.
- हे + माझं + पुस्तक + आहे = हे माझं पुस्तक आहे। — This is my book.
- तो + माझा + भाऊ + आहे = तो माझा भाऊ आहे। — He is my brother.
- आम्ही + शाळेत + जातो = आम्ही शाळेत जातो। — We go to school.

## Negative Sentences

Add **नाही (nāhī)** to negate:

- मी विद्यार्थी आहे। → मी विद्यार्थी **नाही**। — I am not a student.
- तो डॉक्टर आहे। → तो डॉक्टर **नाही**। — He is not a doctor.
- मी जातो। → मी जात **नाही**। — I don't go.

> **नाही (nāhī)** is the standard negation. It comes at the END of the sentence (after the verb stem). This is different from Hindi's नहीं which comes before the verb.

## Question Words

| Question word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| काय (kāy) | what | हे काय आहे? — What is this? |
| कोण (koṇ) | who | तो कोण आहे? — Who is he? |
| कोठे (koṭhe) | where | तुम्ही कोठे जाता? — Where do you go? |
| कधी (kadhī) | when | तो कधी येईल? — When will he come? |
| कसा (kasā) | how | तुम्ही कसे आहात? — How are you? (to male) |
| का (kā) | why | तुम्ही का जाता? — Why do you go? |
| किती (kitī) | how much/many | तुमचे किती भाऊ आहेत? — How many brothers do you have? |

## Yes/No Questions

Add **का (kā)** at the end:

- तो डॉक्टर आहे। → तो डॉक्टर आहे **का**? — Is he a doctor?
- तुम्ही मराठी आहात। → तुम्ही मराठी आहात **का**? — Are you Marathi?

> Marathi puts the question particle **का (kā)** at the END of the sentence — this is different from Hindi, which puts क्या at the BEGINNING.

## Practice

Convert these English sentences to Marathi (SOV order):

1. I am a teacher. → मी शिक्षक आहे।
2. She is my sister. → ती माझी बहीण आहे।
3. We eat rice. → आम्ही भात खातो।
4. They are friends. → ते मित्र आहेत।
5. Is this a book? → हे पुस्तक आहे का?

lessons.title: प्रश्न · Questions
lessons.subtitle: Asking questions in Marathi
lessons.content:
# प्रश्न (Questions)

Marathi questions use question words placed after the subject. The question particle **का (kā)** goes at the END for yes/no questions.

## काय (What)

- हे काय आहे? — What is this?
- तुम्ही काय करता? — What do you do?
- तुमचं नाव काय? — What is your name?
- हे पुस्तक काय आहे? — What is this book?

## कोण (Who)

- तो कोण आहे? — Who is he?
- ती कोण आहे? — Who is she?
- ते कोण आहेत? — Who are they?
- हा मुलगा कोण आहे? — Who is this boy?

## कोठे (Where)

- तुम्ही कोठे जाता? — Where do you go?
- तुम्ही कोठून आहात? — Where are you from?
- बाजार कोठे आहे? — Where is the market?
- माझं पुस्तक कोठे आहे? — Where is my book?

> The postposition **-हून (-hūn)** means 'from': कोठून (koṭhūn — from where), मुंबईतून (mumbaītūn — from Mumbai).

## कधी (When)

- तुम्ही कधी येणार? — When will you come?
- तो कधी गेला? — When did he go?
- कधी जेवायचं? — When will we eat?
- सण कधी आहे? — When is the festival?

## कसा / कशी / कसे (How)

'How' changes by gender:

- तुम्ही कसे आहात? — How are you? (to a male, respectful)
- तुम्ही कशी आहात? — How are you? (to a female, respectful)
- तू कसा आहेस? — How are you? (to a male, informal)
- तू कशी आहेस? — How are you? (to a female, informal)

> Marathi 'how' agrees with the gender of the person being addressed: कसा (masculine), कशी (feminine), कसे (neuter/plural). This is similar to Hindi's कैसा/कैसी/कैसे.

## का (Why)

- तुम्ही का जाता? — Why do you go?
- तो का रडतो? — Why does he cry?
- हे का झालं? — Why did this happen?
- मी हे का करावं? — Why should I do this?

> The response usually starts with **कारण (kāraṇ)** — 'because': कारण मला काम आहे। — 'Because I have work.'

## किती (How much / How many)

- हे किती? — How much is this?
- तुमचे किती भाऊ आहेत? — How many brothers do you have?
- चह्यात किती साखर टाकू? — How much sugar should I put in the tea?

## Conversational Example

> **राहुल:** नमस्कार! तुम्ही कोठून आहात?
> **सारा:** मी अमेरिकेतून आले आहे। आणि तुम्ही?
> **राहुल:** मी मुंबईतून आहे। तुम्ही भारतात कधी आलात?
> **सारा:** मी एक आठवड्यापूर्वी आले आहे।
> **राहुल:** भारत तुम्हाला कसा वाटतो?
> **सारा:** खूप छान! लोक खूप मदतगार आहेत।

**Translation:**
> Rahul: Hello! Where are you from?
> Sara: I have come from America. And you?
> Rahul: I am from Mumbai. When did you come to India?
> Sara: I came a week ago.
> Rahul: How does India feel to you?
> Sara: Very nice! People are very helpful.

## Practice

Form questions for these answers:

1. Answer: मी मुंबईतून आहे। → Question: तुम्ही कोठून आहात?
2. Answer: मी शिक्षक आहे। → Question: तुम्ही काय करता?
3. Answer: तो उद्या येईल। → Question: तो कधी येईल?
4. Answer: जेवण खूप छान होतं। → Question: जेवण कसं होतं?

lessons.title: नकार · Negation
lessons.subtitle: नाही, नको — Marathi's negation system
lessons.content:
# नकार (Negation)

Marathi has two main negation words: **नाही (nāhī)** for 'is not' / 'do not', and **नको (nako)** for 'don't want' / 'don't do'. They have different uses.

## नाही (nāhī) — Standard Negation

**नाही** negates statements and questions. It comes at the END of the sentence (after the verb stem):

- मी विद्यार्थी आहे। → मी विद्यार्थी **नाही**। — I am not a student.
- तो डॉक्टर आहे। → तो डॉक्टर **नाही**। — He is not a doctor.
- मी जातो। → मी जात **नाही**। — I don't go.
- ती खाते। → ती खात **नाही**। — She doesn't eat.

> **Marathi difference from Hindi:** Marathi puts नाही at the END (after the verb stem), while Hindi puts नहीं BEFORE the verb. मी जात नाही (Marathi) vs मैं नहीं जाता (Hindi).

## नको (nako) — 'Don't want' / 'Don't do'

**नको** is used for:
1. Saying you don't want something
2. Negative commands (don't do it!)

**Don't want:**
- चहा नको। — I don't want tea.
- पाणी नको। — I don't want water.
- हे पुस्तक नको। — I don't want this book.

**Negative command:**
- जाऊ नको! — Don't go!
- रडू नको। — Don't cry.
- हे खू नको। — Don't eat this.
- काळजी करू नको। — Don't worry.

> **नको** is uniquely Marathi — Hindi uses मत (mat) for negative commands and नहीं चाहिए for 'don't want'. Marathi's नको covers both meanings.

## Comparing नाही and नको

| Negation | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| नाही | Statement negation (at end) | मी जात नाही। — I don't go. |
| नको | Don't want | चहा नको। — I don't want tea. |
| नको | Negative command | जाऊ नको! — Don't go! |

## Negative Responses

- **तुम्ही मराठी आहात का?** → **नाही, मी अमेरिकन आहे।** — Are you Marathi? No, I'm American.
- **तो येईल का?** → **नाही, तो येणार नाही।** — Will he come? No, he won't come.

## Common Negative Phrases

- **माहित नाही (māhit nāhī)** — I don't know
- **काही नाही (kāhī nāhī)** — nothing / it's nothing
- **कोठेही नाही (koṭhehī nāhī)** — nowhere
- **कधीही नाही (kadhīhī nāhī)** — never
- **कोणीही नाही (koṇīhī nāhī)** — nobody

> **कधीही नाही (kadhīhī nāhī)** — 'never' — combines कधीही (ever) with नाही. This parallels Hindi's कभी नहीं but uses Marathi's नाही.

## Practice

Negate these sentences:

1. मी जातो। → मी जात नाही।
2. तो डॉक्टर आहे। → तो डॉक्टर नाही।
3. खा। → खू नको। (Don't eat.)
4. मी चहा पितो। → मी चहा पित नाही।

lessons.title: दैनंदिन दिनचर्या · Daily Routine
lessons.subtitle: Talking about everyday activities
lessons.content:
# दैनंदिन दिनचर्या (Daily Routine)

This lesson covers everyday activities and how to describe a typical day in Marathi.

## Morning Activities

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| सकाळी उठणे | sakāḷī uṭhṇe | to wake up in the morning |
| दात घासणे | dāt ghāsṇe | to brush teeth |
| आंघोळ करणे | ānghoḷ karaṇe | to bathe |
| चहा पिणे | chahā piṇe | to drink tea |
| नाश्ता करणे | nāśtā karaṇe | to have breakfast |
| पूजा करणे | pūjā karaṇe | to pray / worship |

## Daytime Activities

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| शाळेत जाणे | shāḷet jāṇe | to go to school |
| अभ्यास करणे | abhyās karaṇe | to study |
| काम करणे | kām karaṇe | to work |
| दुपारचे जेवण | dupārche jevaṇ | lunch |
| विश्रांती घेणे | viśrāṃtī gheṇe | to rest |

## Evening Activities

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| संध्याकाळी घरी येणे | sandhyākāḷī gharī yeṇe | to come home in the evening |
| जेवण खाणे | jevaṇ khāṇe | to eat dinner |
| टीव्ही पाहणे | ṭīvhī pāhaṇe | to watch TV |
| मित्रांना भेटणे | mitrāñnā bheṭṇe | to meet friends |
| फिरणे | phiraṇe | to stroll / go out |

## Night Activities

| Marathi | Roman | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| रात्रीचे जेवण | rātrīche jevaṇ | dinner |
| झोपणे | jhopaṇe | to sleep |
| पुस्तक वाचणे | pustak vācaṇe | to read a book |
| दिवा बंद करणे | divā band karaṇe | to turn off the light |

## Present Habitual Tense

The present habitual describes regular actions. Verb endings change by gender:

**Male speaker:**
- मी उठतो (mī uṭhto) — I wake up
- मी जातो (mī jāto) — I go
- मी खातो (mī khāto) — I eat

**Female speaker:**
- मी उठते (mī uṭhte) — I wake up
- मी जाते (mī jāte) — I go
- मी खाते (mī khāte) — I eat

**Third person:**
- तो जातो (to jāto) — He goes
- ती जाते (tī jāte) — She goes
- ते जातात (te jātāt) — They go

> Compare to Hindi: मैं जाता हूँ (male) vs मैं जाती हूँ (female). Marathi: मी जातो (male) vs मी जाते (female). The pattern is similar but the endings differ.

## A Sample Daily Routine

> मी रोज सकाळी सहाला उठतो। मग दात घासतो आणि आंघोळ करतो। सातला चहा पितो आणि नाश्ता करतो. आठला शाळेत जातो. दुपारी दोनला जेवतो. संध्याकाळी पाचला घरी येतो. मग खेळतो किंवा टीव्ही पाहतो. रात्री नऊला जेवतो आणि दहाला झोपतो.
>
> I wake up every morning at six. Then I brush my teeth and bathe. At seven I drink tea and have breakfast. At eight I go to school. At two in the afternoon I eat lunch. I come home at five in the evening. Then I play or watch TV. At nine at night I eat dinner and sleep at ten.

## Time Expressions

- **रोज (roz)** — every day / daily
- **सकाळ (sakāḷ)** — morning
- **दुपार (dupār)** — afternoon
- **संध्याकाळ (sandhyākāḷ)** — evening
- **रात्री (rātrī)** — night
- **आज (āj)** — today
- **उद्या (udyā)** — tomorrow
- **काल (kāl)** — yesterday
- **आता (ātā)** — now

## Talking About Time

- **किती वाजले? (kitī vājle?)** — What time is it? (lit: how many struck)
- **सकाळी सहाला (sakāḷī sahālā)** — at six in the morning
- **दुपारी दोनला (dupārī donlā)** — at two in the afternoon
- **रात्री दहाला (rātrī dahālā)** — at ten at night

> The postposition **-ला (-lā)** marks time: सहाला (at six o'clock), दोनला (at two). This is the same postposition used for indirect objects.

## Practice

Describe your daily routine using the template:

> मी रोज सकाळी _____ला उठतो/उठते। मग _____। शाळेत/कामाला _____ला जातो/जाते। संध्याकाळी _____। रात्री _____ला झोपतो/झोपते।

lessons.title: सर्वनाम · Pronouns
lessons.subtitle: Marathi pronouns — तू, तुम्ही, आपण, तो, ती, ते
lessons.content:
# सर्वनाम (Pronouns)

Marathi pronouns distinguish THREE levels of 'you' (तू, तुम्ही, आपण) and THREE third-person genders (तो, ती, ते). The system is similar to Hindi but with Marathi-specific words.

## Personal Pronouns

| Person | Direct | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1st sg | मी (mī) | I |
| 1st pl | आम्ही (āmhī) | we (exclusive) |
| 1st pl | आपण (āpaṇ) | we (inclusive) |
| 2nd intimate | तू (tū) | you (intimate) |
| 2nd familiar | तुम्ही (tumhī) | you (familiar/respectful) |
| 2nd formal | आपण (āpaṇ) | you (very formal) |
| 3rd sg masc | तो (to) | he |
| 3rd sg fem | ती (tī) | she |
| 3rd sg neut | ते (te) | it |
| 3rd pl | ते (te) | they |

## The Three 'You's

1. **तू (tū)** — intimate. For close friends, younger family, children. Takes singular verb.
2. **तुम्ही (tumhī)** — familiar/respectful. For peers, elders, strangers. Takes plural verb.
3. **आपण (āpaṇ)** — very formal. For elders, in-laws, respected figures. Takes plural verb.

> **Marathi vs Hindi:** Hindi uses तू/तुम/आप. Marathi uses तू/तुम्ही/आपण. The pattern is the same, but the words are different. Note: Marathi's तुम्ही is more commonly used than Hindi's तुम — it carries respect.

## The Inclusive vs Exclusive 'We'

Marathi distinguishes TWO forms of 'we':

- **आम्ही (āmhī)** — exclusive 'we' (excludes the listener): "We (but not you) are going."
- **आपण (āpaṇ)** — inclusive 'we' (includes the listener): "We (you and I) are going."

> This distinction exists in Marathi but not in standard Hindi (which uses हम for both). It's a feature Marathi shares with Tamil, Telugu, and other Dravidian languages.

## Third Person: Three Genders

Marathi third-person singular pronouns mark gender:

- **तो (to)** — he (masculine)
- **ती (tī)** — she (feminine)
- **ते (te)** — it (neuter) / they (plural)

> Marathi's NEUTER gender is distinctive — Hindi has only masculine and feminine. ते can mean 'it' (singular neuter) or 'they' (plural). Context determines which.

## Possessive Forms

| Pronoun | Possessive | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| मी (I) | माझा / माझी / माझं (mājhā/mājhī/mājhaṃ) | my (m/f/n) |
| आम्ही (we) | आमचा / आमची / आमचं (āmchā/āmchī/āmchaṃ) | our |
| तू (you inf.) | तुझा / तुझी / तुझं (tujhā/tujhī/tujhaṃ) | your |
| तुम्ही (you resp.) | तुमचा / तुमची / तुमचं (tumchā/tumchī/tumchaṃ) | your |
| तो (he) | त्याचा / त्याची / त्याचं (tyāchā/tyāchī/tyāchaṃ) | his |
| ती (she) | तिचा / तिची / तिचं (tichā/tichī/tichaṃ) | her |
| ते (it/they) | त्यांचा / त्यांची / त्यांचं (tyāñchā/tyāñchī/tyāñchaṃ) | its/their |

> The possessive changes by the GENDER of the thing possessed: माझा भाऊ (my brother — masc), माझी बहीण (my sister — fem), माझं नाव (my name — neut). This is similar to Hindi's मेरा/मेरी but with three forms instead of two.

## Oblique Forms

When a pronoun is followed by a postposition, it takes the oblique form:

- मी + ला → मला (malā — to me)
- तू + ला → तुला (tulā — to you)
- तो + ला → त्याला (tyālā — to him)
- ती + ला → तिला (tilā — to her)
- आम्ही + ला → आम्हाला (āmhālā — to us)
- तुम्ही + ला → तुम्हाला (tumhālā — to you)

## Using Pronouns in Sentences

- **मी पुस्तक वाचतो।** — I read a book. (male)
- **तुम्ही कोठे जाता?** — Where do you go?
- **तो माझा मित्र आहे।** — He is my friend.
- **मला चहा द्या।** — Please give me tea.
- **त्याने मला बोलावलं।** — He called me.

## Practice

Fill in the correct pronoun:

1. _____ घरी जातो। (I go home.) → मी
2. _____ नाव काय? (What is your name, respectful?) → तुमचं
3. _____ भेटण्याचा आनंद आहे। (Nice to meet you.) → तुमच्या
4. _____ ला जेवण द्या। (Give him food.) → त्याला
5. _____ भाऊ डॉक्टर आहे। (My brother is a doctor.) → माझा

lessons.title: लिंग · Three Genders
lessons.subtitle: Marathi's distinctive three-gender system
lessons.content:
# लिंग (Gender)

**Marathi has THREE grammatical genders: masculine (पुल्लिंग), feminine (स्त्रीलिंग), and NEUTER (नपुंसकलिंग).** This is a key difference from Hindi, which has only two. The neuter gender is one of Marathi's most distinctive features.

## The Three Genders

### Masculine (पुल्लिंग)
- तो मुलगा (to mulgā) — that boy
- तो भाऊ (to bhāu) — that brother
- तो शिक्षक (to shikṣak) — that teacher (male)

### Feminine (स्त्रीलिंग)
- ती मुलगी (tī mulgī) — that girl
- ती बहीण (tī bahīṇ) — that sister
- ती शिक्षिका (tī shikṣikā) — that teacher (female)

### Neuter (नपुंसकलिंग) — Marathi's Distinctive Gender
- ते पुस्तक (te pustak) — that book
- ते नाव (te nāv) — that name
- ते घर (te ghar) — that house
- ते पाणी (te pāṇī) — that water

> The neuter gender is what sets Marathi apart from Hindi. In Hindi, पुस्तक (book) is feminine, घर (house) is masculine, पानी (water) is masculine. In Marathi, these are all NEUTER. This affects verb agreement.

## Gender Patterns

### Masculine Endings
- Words ending in -आ (-ā): मुलगा (boy), बाबा (father)
- Words ending in -कार (-kār): शिक्षक (teacher), कलाकार (artist)
- Words for male humans/animals

### Feminine Endings
- Words ending in -ई (-ī): मुलगी (girl), बहीण (sister)
- Words ending in -आन (-ān) in Sanskrit loans: शिक्षिका (teacher f)
- Words for female humans/animals

### Neuter Endings
- Words ending in -अं (-aṃ): नावं (name), घरं (house — colloquial)
- Abstract nouns: ज्ञान (knowledge), प्रेम (love)
- Many natural objects: पुस्तक (book), पाणी (water), फूल (flower)

> **The neuter gender is everywhere in Marathi.** Many common nouns that are masculine or feminine in Hindi are NEUTER in Marathi. This is the single biggest grammar adjustment for Hindi speakers learning Marathi.

## Verb Agreement with Gender

Marathi verbs agree with the subject's gender. With THREE genders, there are three verb forms:

| Subject gender | Present tense ending | Example (जाणे = to go) |
|---|---|---|
| Masculine sg | -तो (-to) | मी जातो (I go — male) |
| Feminine sg | -ते (-te) | मी जाते (I go — female) |
| Neuter sg | -ते (-te) | ते जाते (it goes) |
| Plural | -तात (-tāt) | ते जातात (they go) |

> Note: feminine singular and neuter singular have the SAME verb ending (-ते). This is a coincidence that simplifies learning slightly.

## Adjective Agreement

Adjectives also agree with the noun's gender:

**Masculine:**
- छान मुलगा (chhān mulgā) — good boy
- छान शिक्षक (chhān shikṣak) — good teacher (m)

**Feminine:**
- छान मुलगी (chhān mulgī) — good girl
- छान शिक्षिका (chhān shikṣikā) — good teacher (f)

**Neuter:**
- छान पुस्तक (chhān pustak) — good book
- छान घर (chhān ghar) — good house

> Many Marathi adjectives (like छान) are INVARIABLE — they don't change by gender. This is simpler than Hindi's अच्छा/अच्छी/अच्छे system.

## Common Neuter Nouns

These nouns are NEUTER in Marathi but NOT in Hindi:

| Marathi (neuter) | Hindi gender | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| पुस्तक (pustak) | feminine | book |
| घर (ghar) | masculine | house |
| पाणी (pāṇī) | masculine | water |
| नाव (nāv) | masculine | name |
| फूल (phūl) | masculine | flower |
| दरवाजा (darvājā) | masculine | door |
| शहर (shahar) | masculine | city |

> If you know Hindi, you need to RE-LEARN the gender of these nouns. They're neuter in Marathi, not masculine or feminine. This is the biggest grammar challenge for Hindi speakers.

## The Neuter Verb Ending

When the subject is neuter, the verb takes the neuter ending:

- पुस्तक आहे (pustak ahe) — the book is (neuter)
- घर आहे (ghar ahe) — the house is (neuter)
- पाणी आहे (pāṇī ahe) — the water is (neuter)

> Note: आहे (ahe) is used for both masculine and neuter singular subjects. The difference shows in the pronoun: तो आहे (he is) vs ते आहे (it is).

## Practice

Identify the gender and use the correct pronoun:

1. _____ मुलगा (boy) → तो (masculine)
2. _____ मुलगी (girl) → ती (feminine)
3. _____ पुस्तक (book) → ते (neuter — Marathi distinctive!)
4. _____ घर (house) → ते (neuter — Marathi distinctive!)
5. _____ पाणी (water) → ते (neuter — Marathi distinctive!)

lessons.title: काळ · Tenses
lessons.subtitle: Present, past, and future tenses in Marathi
lessons.content:
# काळ (Tenses)

Marathi has three main tenses: present (वर्तमान काळ), past (भूत काळ), and future (भविष्य काळ). Verbs conjugate by person, number, and gender.

## Present Habitual (वर्तमान काळ)

Describes regular actions. Verb stem + gender/number ending:

| Subject | Masculine | Feminine | Neuter/Plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| मी (I) | जातो (jāto) | जाते (jāte) | — |
| तू (you inf.) | जातोस (jātos) | जातेस (jātes) | — |
| तुम्ही (you resp.) | जाता (jātā) | जाता (jātā) | — |
| तो (he) | जातो (jāto) | — | — |
| ती (she) | — | जाते (jāte) | — |
| ते (it/they) | — | — | जातात (jātāt) |
| आम्ही (we) | जातो (jāto) | जातो (jāto) | — |

**Examples:**
- मी रोज शाळेत जातो। — I go to school every day. (male)
- मी रोज शाळेत जाते। — I go to school every day. (female)
- ती चहा पिते। — She drinks tea.
- ते पुस्तक वाचतात। — They read books. (or: It reads — neuter pl)

## Past Tense (भूत काळ)

Past tense adds -ल- (-l-) before the ending:

| Subject | Masculine | Feminine | Neuter |
|---|---|---|---|
| मी (I) | गेलो (gelo) | गेले (gele) | — |
| तू (you inf.) | गेलास (gelās) | गेलीस (gelīs) | — |
| तो (he) | गेला (gelā) | — | — |
| ती (she) | — | गेली (gelī) | — |
| ते (it/they) | — | — | गेलं (gelaṃ) / गेली (gelī) |

**Examples:**
- मी काल बाजारात गेलो। — I went to the market yesterday. (male)
- मी काल बाजारात गेले। — I went to the market yesterday. (female)
- ती घरी आली। — She came home.
- ते गेलं। — It went. (neuter)

> **Marathi past tense doesn't use a ने marker** like Hindi's मैंने. Marathi: मी गेलो (I went). Hindi: मैं गया था. This is simpler than Hindi.

## Future Tense (भविष्य काळ)

Future tense adds -ईल- (-īl-) or -नार- (-nār-):

| Subject | Masculine | Feminine |
|---|---|---|
| मी (I) | जेन (yen) | जेन (yen) |
| तू (you inf.) | जेशील (yeśīl) | जेशील (yeśīl) |
| तुम्ही (you resp.) | जाल (jāl) | जाल (jāl) |
| तो (he) | येईल (yeīl) | — |
| ती (she) | — | येईल (yeīl) |
| ते (it/they) | — | येतील (yetīl) |

**Examples:**
- मी उद्या येन। — I will come tomorrow.
- तो संध्याकाळी जाईल। — He will go in the evening.
- आम्ही रविवारी येऊ। — We will come on Sunday.

## Tense Comparison

| Tense | Pattern (1st masc) | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Present | stem + -तो | मी जातो (I go) |
| Past | stem + -लो | मी गेलो (I went) |
| Future | stem + -एन | मी जेन (I will go) |

## Common Time Markers

**Present:**
- रोज (roz) — daily
- नेहमी (nehmī) — always
- बहुतांशी (bahutāñśī) — mostly

**Past:**
- काल (kāl) — yesterday
- गेल्या आठवड्यात (gelyā āṭhvadyāt) — last week
- आधी (ādhī) — before

**Future:**
- उद्या (udyā) — tomorrow
- पुढच्या आठवड्यात (puḍhachyā āṭhvadyāt) — next week
- नंतर (ntar) — later

## Practice

Convert these sentences to the tense in brackets:

1. मी जातो। (past) → मी गेलो।
2. ती खाते। (future) → ती खाईल।
3. मी वाचलो। (present) → मी वाचतो।
4. आम्ही आलो। (future) → आम्ही येऊ।
5. ते खेळतात। (past) → ते खेळले।

lessons.subtitle: Marathi postpositions: ला, ने, चा/ची/चे, मध्ये
lessons.content:
# शब्दयोगी अव्यय (Postpositions)

Marathi uses postpositions (not prepositions) — they come AFTER the noun. Marathi's postposition system is similar to Hindi's but with distinct forms.

## The Core Postpositions

| Postposition | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ला (lā) | to (recipient/time) | मला — to me |
| ने (ne) | by (agent in past) | त्याने — by him |
| चा / ची / चे (chā/chī/che) | of (possessive) | माझा — my |
| मध्ये (madhye) | in / inside | घरामध्ये — in the house |
| वर (var) | on / above | टेबलावर — on the table |
| खाली (khālī) | under / below | टेबलाखाली — under the table |
| हून (hūn) | from | मुंबईहून — from Mumbai |
| कडे (kaḍe) | towards / to (direction) | घराकडे — towards home |
| सोबत (sobat) | with (accompaniment) | माझ्यासोबत — with me |
| साठी (sāṭhī) | for | तुमच्यासाठी — for you |
| बद्दल (baddal) | about | तुमच्याबद्दल — about you |

## ला (lā) — To

ला marks recipient or time:

- मला (malā) — to me
- तुला (tulā) — to you
- त्याला (tyālā) — to him
- तिला (tilā) — to her
- रामला (rām-lā) — to Ram
- सकाळी सहाला (sakāḷī sahālā) — at six in the morning

**Examples:**
- मला चहा द्या। — Give me tea.
- त्याला सांगा। — Tell him.
- तो सहाला येईल। — He will come at six.

> ला is used for BOTH indirect objects (to him) AND time expressions (at six). This dual use is distinctive to Marathi.

## ने (ne) — Agent in Past Tense

In the past tense, the subject of a transitive verb takes ने:

- त्याने (tyāne) — he (as agent)
- तिने (tine) — she (as agent)
- मीने / माझ्याने (mīne / mājhyāne) — I (as agent)
- रामाने (rāmāne) — Ram (as agent)

**Examples:**
- त्याने पुस्तक वाचलं। — He read a book.
- तिने चहा पिला। — She drank tea.
- मीने जेवण केलं। — I made food.

> This is similar to Hindi's ने marker (उसने, मैंने), but Marathi uses it consistently for transitive past-tense subjects.

## चा / ची / चे (Possessive)

The possessive changes by the GENDER of the thing possessed:

- चा (chā) — masculine singular: माझा भाऊ (my brother)
- ची (chī) — feminine: माझी बहीण (my sister)
- चे (che) — neuter / plural: माझं नाव (my name), माझे भाऊ (my brothers)

**Examples:**
- रामचा भाऊ (rām-chā bhāu) — Ram's brother
- रामची बहीण (rām-chī bahīṇ) — Ram's sister
- रामचं नाव (rām-chaṃ nāv) — Ram's name

> The possessive agrees with the noun it PRECEDES (the thing possessed), with THREE forms (चा/ची/चे) matching Marathi's three genders.

## मध्ये (madhye) — In

- घरामध्ये (gharāmadhye) — in the house
- शाळेमध्ये (shāḷemadhye) — in the school
- पुस्तकामध्ये (pustakāmadhye) — in the book
- मुंबईमध्ये (mumbaimadhye) — in Mumbai

## वर (var) — On

- टेबलावर (ṭebalāvar) — on the table
- खुर्चीवर (khurchīvar) — on the chair
- छतावर (chatāvar) — on the roof
- भिंतीवर (bhintīvar) — on the wall

## हून (hūn) — From

- मुंबईहून (mumbaihūn) — from Mumbai
- पुण्याहून (puṇyāhūn) — from Pune
- बाजाराहून (bājārāhūn) — from the market
- आमेरिकेहून (āmerikehūn) — from America

> हून is Marathi's 'from' postposition — different from Hindi's से. मुंबईहून (Marathi) vs मुंबई से (Hindi).

## Compound Postpositions

- **-च्या मध्ये (-chyā madhye)** — in: घराच्या मध्ये — in the house
- **-च्या वर (-chyā var)** — on: टेबलाच्या वर — on the table
- **-च्या खाली (-chyā khālī)** — under: टेबलाच्या खाली — under the table
- **-च्या सोबत (-chyā sobat)** — with: माझ्या सोबत — with me
- **-च्या साठी (-chyā sāṭhī)** — for: तुमच्या साठी — for you

## Possession — कडे (kaḍe)

To express 'I have', Marathi uses **कडे (kaḍe)** — 'near/towards':

- माझ्याकडे पुस्तक आहे। — I have a book. (lit: towards me book is)
- त्याच्याकडे पैसे आहेत। — He has money.
- तुमच्याकडे वेळ आहे का? — Do you have time?

> This is similar to Hindi's पास construction (मेरे पास किताब है), but Marathi uses कडे (towards) instead of पास (near).

## Practice

Translate to Marathi:

1. in the house → घरामध्ये
2. on the table → टेबलावर
3. from Mumbai → मुंबईहून
4. to me → मला
5. for you → तुमच्यासाठी
6. with me → माझ्यासोबत
7. under the chair → खुर्चीखाली
8. Ram's book → रामचं पुस्तक (neuter!)

# संवाद (Conversations)

This lesson presents three dialogues that bring together everything you've learned. Read them aloud to practise pronunciation.

## Dialogue 1: Meeting a New Neighbour

> **राहुल:** नमस्कार! मी राहुल, शेजारच्या फ्लॅटमध्ये राहतो.
> **श्रीमती शर्मा:** नमस्कार! मी शर्मा बोलते, हा माझा नवरा. तुम्ही इथे नवीन आहात?
> **राहुल:** होय, मी एक आठवड्यापूर्वी शिफ्ट झालो. मी मुंबईहून आले आहे.
> **श्रीमती शर्मा:** अरे, मुंबईहून! तिथे कसं होतं?
> **राहुल:** खूप छान, पण नोकरीमुळे पुण्यात यावं लागलं. तुम्ही कधीपासून इथे आहात?
> **श्रीमती शर्मा:** गेल्या वीस वर्षांपासून. हे आमचं स्वतःचं घर आहे. काही हवं असेल तर सांगा.
> **राहुल:** धन्यवाद! नक्की सांगेन.

**Translation:**
> Rahul: Hello! I'm Rahul, I live in the next flat.
> Mrs. Sharma: Hello! I'm Sharma speaking, this is my husband. Are you new here?
> Rahul: Yes, I shifted a week ago. I came from Mumbai.
> Mrs. Sharma: Oh, from Mumbai! How was it there?
> Rahul: Very nice, but I had to come to Pune for work. How long have you been here?
> Mrs. Sharma: For the last twenty years. This is our own house. Let me know if you need anything.
> Rahul: Thank you! I will surely tell.

## Dialogue 2: At the Vegetable Shop

> **विक्रम:** भाऊ, बटाटे कितीला?
> **दुकानदार:** वीस रुपये किलो, नक्की.
> **विक्रम:** थोडं जास्त आहे. पंचवीसात दोन किलो दे.
> **दुकानदार:** नाही भाऊ, ते होणार नाही. घे, तीसात दोन किलो.
> **विक्रम:** ठीक आहे, दोन किलो बटाटे दे. आणि कांदे एक किलो. कांदे कितीला?
> **दुकानदार:** कांदे चाळीस रुपये किलो.
> **विक्रम:** मग सत्तर रुपये झाले. हे घे शंभर, उरलेले परत दे.
> **दुकानदार:** हे घे तीस रुपये. आणखी काही?
> **विक्रम:** नाही, एवढंच. धन्यवाद!

**Translation:**
> Vikram: Brother, how much are the potatoes?
> Shopkeeper: Twenty rupees a kilo, fixed.
> Vikram: A bit much. Give two kilos for twenty-five.
> Shopkeeper: No brother, that won't work. Take it, two kilos for thirty.
> Vikram: OK, give two kilos of potatoes. And one kilo of onions. How much are onions?
> Shopkeeper: Onions are forty rupees a kilo.
> Vikram: Then that's seventy rupees. Here's one hundred, give the change.
> Shopkeeper: Here's thirty rupees. Anything else?
> Vikram: No, just this. Thanks!

## Dialogue 3: Planning a Trip to Shirdi

> **प्रिया:** रविवारी काय करत आहेस?
> **अमित:** काही खास नाही. का?
> **प्रिया:** शिरडीला चलूया? साईबाबाचं दर्शन करायला?
> **अमित:** छान कल्पना! कसं जाऊ — ट्रेनने की गाडीने?
> **प्रिया:** गाडीने गेलो तर वाटेत नाशिकही पाहू शकू.
> **अमित:** बरोबर सांगितलंस. कधी निघायचं?
> **प्रिया:** सकाळी सहाला. दहाला शिरडीला पोहोचू.
> **अमित:** आणि जेवण?
> **प्रिया:** वाटेत कुठेतरी थांबू. तू येशील ना?
> **अमित:** होय, येईन. रविवारी सकाळी सहाला भेटूया.

**Translation:**
> Priya: What are you doing on Sunday?
> Amit: Nothing special. Why?
> Priya: Shall we go to Shirdi? To have darshan of Sai Baba?
> Amit: Nice idea! How should we go — by train or by car?
> Priya: If we go by car, we can also see Nashik on the way.
> Amit: Right. When should we leave?
> Priya: At six in the morning. We'll reach Shirdi by ten.
> Amit: And food?
> Priya: We'll stop somewhere on the way. You'll come, right?
> Amit: Yes, I'll come. Let's meet Sunday at six in the morning.

## Cultural Note: Shirdi

**शिरडी (Shirdi)** is a town in Maharashtra, home to **साईबाबा (Sai Baba)** — one of India's most revered saints. Sai Baba's teachings emphasized unity of all religions. Millions of devotees visit Shirdi each year, making it one of Maharashtra's most important pilgrimage sites.

## Practice

Read each dialogue aloud three times. Then cover the Marathi and try to reconstruct it from the English.

# परिच्छेद वाचन (Reading Paragraphs)

This lesson presents three short paragraphs on Marathi culture, each followed by comprehension questions.

## Passage 1: मुंबई (Mumbai)

> मी मुंबईत राहतो. मुंबई महाराष्ट्राची राजधानी आहे. याला 'आर्थिक राजधानी' देखील म्हणतात. या शहरात गेटवे ऑफ इंडिया, मरीन ड्राईव्ह, छत्रपती शिवाजी महाराज टर्मिनस, आणि सिद्धिविनायक मंदिरासारखी प्रसिद्ध ठिकाणे आहेत. मुंबईला 'नगरी ज्यातून जडल्या स्वप्ने' असंही म्हणतात — कारण या शहरात प्रत्येकाची स्वप्न पूर्ण होतात. गणेशोत्सव हा इ�ला सर्वात मोठा सण आहे — भाद्रपद महिन्यात पूरं शहर गणपतीच्या प्रतिमांनी सजतं. मुंबईचं खाणंही प्रसिद्ध आहे — वडापाव, पावभाजी, मिसळपाव, आणि चिवडा. इथले लोक खूप मेहनती आणि जिद्दीदार आहेत.

**Translation:**
> I live in Mumbai. Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra. It is also called the 'financial capital'. This city has famous places like Gateway of India, Marine Drive, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, and Siddhivinayak Temple. Mumbai is also called 'the city where dreams are woven' — because in this city, everyone's dreams come true. Ganesh festival is the biggest festival here — in the Bhadrapad month, the whole city is decorated with Ganesh idols. Mumbai's food is also famous — vada pav, pav bhaji, misal pav, and chivda. The people here are very hardworking and determined.

**Comprehension questions:**
1. मुंबई कोणत्या राज्याची राजधानी आहे? (Mumbai is the capital of which state?)
2. मुंबईला काय म्हणतात? (What is Mumbai called?)
3. मुंबईतील काही प्रसिद्ध ठिकाणे सांगा। (Name some famous places in Mumbai.)
4. मुंबईतील सर्वात मोठा सण कोणता? (What is the biggest festival in Mumbai?)
5. मुंबईचे काही प्रसिद्ध खाणपदार्थ सांगा। (Name some famous foods of Mumbai.)

## Passage 2: गणेशोत्सव (Ganesh Festival)

> गणेशोत्सव हा महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात मोठा सण आहे. भाद्रपद महिन्यात हा सण साजरा केला जातो. लोक घरी किंवा सार्वजनिक मंडळांमध्ये गणपतीची मूर्ती स्थापन करतात. दहा दिवस हा उत्सव चालतो — दररोज पूजा, आरती, आणि प्रसाद वाटला जातो. गणेशोत्सवात लोक गाणी गातात, नाच करतात, आणि मित्रांना भेटतात. अनंत चतुर्दशीला गणपतीची मूर्ती पाण्यात विसर्जित केली जाते — याला 'गणेश विसर्जन' म्हणतात. लोक 'गणपती बाप्पा मोरया, पुढच्या वर्षी लवकर या' अशी घोषणा देतात. हा सण एकता आणि भक्तीचा प्रतीक आहे.

**Translation:**
> Ganesh festival is the biggest festival in Maharashtra. It is celebrated in the Bhadrapad month. People install Ganesh idols at home or in public mandals. The festival lasts for ten days — daily puja, aarti, and prasad are offered. During Ganesh festival, people sing songs, dance, and meet friends. On Anant Chaturdashi, the Ganesh idol is immersed in water — this is called 'Ganesh Visarjan'. People shout 'Ganapati Bappa Morya, come again next year soon'. This festival is a symbol of unity and devotion.

**Comprehension questions:**
1. गणेशोत्सव कोणत्या महिन्यात साजरा केला जातो? (In which month is Ganesh festival celebrated?)
2. उत्सव किती दिवस चालतो? (How many days does the festival last?)
3. गणेश विसर्जन कधी होतं? (When does Ganesh visarjan happen?)
4. लोक काय घोषणा देतात? (What slogan do people shout?)
5. हा सण कशाचा प्रतीक आहे? (What is this festival a symbol of?)

## Passage 3: मराठी खाणं (Marathi Food)

> मराठी खाणं खूप छान आणि विविध प्रकारचं आहे. भात आणि भाकरी हे मराठी जेवणाचे मुख्य पदार्थ आहेत. भाजी, आमटी, पापड, आणि लोणचं हे रोजच्या�ेवणाचे भाग आहेत. महाराष्ट्रात विविध प्रकारच्या भाकऱ्या बनतात — ज्वारीची, बाजरीची, आणि तांदळाची. चटणी आणि ठेचलेलं कांदे हे जेवणाचे वैशिष्ट्य आहे. मराठी खाण्यात गोड पदार्थही प्रसिद्ध आहेत — पुरणपोळी, मोदक, आणि श्रीखंड. चहा हे मराठी लोकांचे आवडते पेय आहे — सकाळी आणि संध्याकाळी चहा पिणं एक दिनचर्या बनली आहे. प्रत्येक प्रांतात खाण्याची वेगळी शैली आहे — कोकणात नारळाचा वापर जास्त, विदर्भात मसाल्याचा.

**Translation:**
> Marathi food is very delicious and diverse. Rice and bhakari (flatbread) are the main items of a Marathi meal. Bhaji (vegetable), amti (dal), papad, and pickle are parts of daily meals. In Maharashtra, various types of bhakari are made — jowar, bajra, and rice. Chutney and crushed onions are characteristic of the meal. Marathi food also has famous sweets — puran poli, modak, and shrikhand. Tea is the favorite drink of Marathi people — drinking tea in the morning and evening has become a routine. Each region has a different style of cooking — Konkan uses more coconut, Vidarbha uses more spices.

**Comprehension questions:**
1. मराठी जेवणाचे मुख्य पदार्थ काय आहेत? (What are the main items of a Marathi meal?)
2. भाकरी कशाची बनते? (What is bhakari made of?)
3. मराठी गोड पदार्थांची नावे सांगा। (Name Marathi sweets.)
4. मराठी लोकांचे आवडते पेय काय आहे? (What is the favorite drink of Marathi people?)
5. कोकण आणि विदर्भात खाण्यात काय फरक आहे? (What is the difference between Konkan and Vidarbha food?)

# पुनरावलोकन (Review)

This lesson reviews everything you've learned across all five levels of Marathi.

## Level 0 Review: Script

**Identify the distinctive Marathi sound:**
- काळ → ळ (ḷ) — retroflex lateral, unique to Marathi
- फळ → ळ
- बाळ → ळ

**Read these words:**
- नमस्कार (namaskār) — hello
- भाजी (bhājī) — vegetable
- पोळी (poḷī) — flatbread
- काळ (kāḷ) — time

## Level 1 Review: Greetings & Introductions

**Greet someone:**
- Respectful: नमस्कार
- Time-specific: शुभ सकाळ (morning), शुभ रात्री (night)

**Introduce yourself:**
- माझं नाव _____ आहे।
- मी _____-त राहतो/राहते।
- मी _____ आहे।

**Marathi kinship:**
- आई (mother), बाबा (father)
- आजी (grandmother), आजोबा (grandfather)
- भाऊ (brother), बहीण (sister)

**Numbers — distinctive Marathi:**
- 5 = पंच (not Hindi's पाँच)
- 6 = षण्ण (not Hindi's छह!)
- 100 = शंभर (not Hindi's सौ)

## Level 2 Review: Daily Life

**Form sentences (SOV order):**
- I eat rice. → मी भात खातो। (male) / मी भात खाते। (female)
- She drinks tea. → ती चहा पिते।
- We go home. → आम्ही घरी जातो।

**Ask questions:**
- What is this? → हे काय आहे?
- Where is the market? → बाजार कोठे आहे?
- When will you come? → तुम्ही कधी येणार?

**Negate:**
- Statement: मी जात नाही। (I don't go — नाही at end)
- Command: जाऊ नको! (Don't go — नको)
- Don't want: चहा नको। (I don't want tea)

## Level 3 Review: Grammar

**Marathi's THREE genders (distinctive!):**
- Masculine: तो मुलगा (that boy)
- Feminine: ती मुलगी (that girl)
- Neuter: ते पुस्तक (that book) — Marathi distinctive!

**Neuter nouns (different from Hindi):**
- पुस्तक (book) — neuter in Marathi, feminine in Hindi
- घर (house) — neuter in Marathi, masculine in Hindi
- पाणी (water) — neuter in Marathi, masculine in Hindi

**Verb conjugation (gender-based):**
- Present: मी जातो (male), मी जाते (female)
- Past: मी गेलो (male), मी गेले (female)
- Future: मी जेन (I will go)

**Postpositions:**
- in the house → घरामध्ये
- on the table → टेबलावर
- from Mumbai → मुंबईहून
- to me → मला
- for you → तुमच्यासाठी

## Level 4 Review: Reading

**Read this passage and answer:**

> आज रविवार आहे. मी सकाळी उठलो, आंघोळ केली, चहा पिला. मग नाश्ता केला — पोह्या आणि चटणी. दहाला बाजारात गेलो. तिथून भाजी आणि फळं आणली. दुपारी जेवलो आणि विश्रांती घेतली. संध्याकाळी मित्रांना भेटलो. आम्ही बागेत फिरलो. रात्री टीव्ही पाहिला आणि झोपलो. उद्या सोमवार आहे, परत कामाला जायला लागेल.

**Questions:**
1. आज कोणता दिवस आहे? (What day is today?)
2. लेखकाने नाश्त्यात काय खाल्लं? (What did the writer eat for breakfast?)
3. तो दहाला कोठे गेला? (Where did he go at ten?)
4. संध्याकाळी त्याने काय केलं? (What did he do in the evening?)
5. उद्या कोणता दिवस आहे? (What day is tomorrow?)

## Self-Assessment Checklist

- [ ] I can read Devanagari script, including Marathi's distinctive ळ
- [ ] I can greet people with नमस्कार and introduce myself
- [ ] I can form simple SOV sentences with gender agreement
- [ ] I can ask and answer questions
- [ ] I can negate with नाही and नको
- [ ] I understand the THREE-gender system (masculine, feminine, neuter)
- [ ] I know the distinctive Marathi number words (षण्ण, शंभर)
- [ ] I can use Marathi postpositions (ला, ने, चा/ची/चे, मध्ये, वर, हून)
- [ ] I can conjugate verbs in present, past, and future tenses
- [ ] I can read short paragraphs with comprehension

## Marathi vs Hindi — Key Differences

If you know Hindi, these are the biggest adjustments:

1. **THREE genders** (Marathi has neuter; Hindi doesn't)
2. **ळ sound** (Hindi uses ल; Marathi has both ल and ळ)
3. **Different pronouns** (तुम्ही vs तुम, आपण vs आप)
4. **नाही at END** (Hindi's नहीं comes before verb)
5. **नको** for 'don't want' / 'don't do' (Hindi uses separate words)
6. **-हून for 'from'** (Hindi uses से)
7. **-ला for 'to' and time** (Hindi uses को and बजे)
8. **Different number words** (षण्ण=6, शंभर=100)
9. **Different kinship** (आई vs माँ, बाबा vs पापा)
10. **Different vocabulary** (भाजी vs सब्ज़ी, पोळी vs रोटी)

## What's Next

This course covered Levels 0-4 (script foundation through intermediate). To continue:

1. **Practice daily:** Even 15 minutes a day keeps the language fresh
2. **Watch Marathi content:** Marathi cinema, Sangeet Marathi channel, Marathi news
3. **Read Marathi literature:** Start with Kusumagraj, P. L. Deshpande, then modern authors
4. **Listen to Marathi music:** Bhavageet, Natya Sangeet, modern Marathi songs
5. **Visit Maharashtra:** Mumbai, Pune, Konkan — immersion accelerates learning

> शुभेच्छा! (Congratulations!) You've completed the VaaniX Marathi Learn Mode course. मराठी सोबत राहा! (Stay with Marathi!)
